title: Canonical derived cups for discrete-lattice equivariant algebras
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring on the small coherent profinite site [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], [def-weil-size-convention], and use internal modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and internal actions [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. For $r\geq0$, use the ordinary discrete lattice action category $\mathcal E=\operatorname{Action}(\operatorname{Mod}_R,\mathbf Z^r)$, its actual invariant limit $\Gamma$ and its total right derived functor $R\Gamma$ from [lem-sfb-discrete-lattice-koszul-resolution], in the ordinary derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with the canonical derived invariants calculus of [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus]. Use the normalized derived adjunction and tensor of [def-sfb-lattice-derived-invariants-tensor]. Define the trivial-action functor $t$ by the identity action, and take its adjunction with $\Gamma$ normalized so that inverse transpose is composition with the invariant inclusion. Use the unique comparison from the recorded total derived functor to the universal right-derived functor preserving the computation unit. Derive this adjunction with exact left adjoint $t$. Equip $D(t)$ with the unique strong tensor structure whose comparison on flat K-flat cochain representatives is localization of the ordinary identity tensor comparison, and whose unit is the localization of the ordinary tensor unit. Give $R\Gamma$ the resulting right-adjoint lax tensor structure: its binary map is the mate of the tensor of the two counits. For an equivariant internal unital $R$-algebra $B$ (a monoid object in $\mathcal E$, commutative when its existing commutativity predicate holds), use the signed total cochain tensor (the existing cochain monoidal tensor) and define $m_B$ on the degree-zero single complex by its original multiplication on the $(0,0)$ tensor summand. Define $\operatorname{cup}_B$ as the lax binary map followed by $R\Gamma$ of the localization tensorator and $m_B$. Define the canonical unit from $R[0]$ by the derived adjunction unit followed by the original equivariant unit of $B$. No flatness of $R$ or $B$, characteristic, or nonzero hypothesis is used in these definitions.
